delete_intro_pairs.item: The user prefers self-blaming apologetic tone when emailing leadership about lost deals with no competitive analysis or lessons learned.
The user always works solo on complex enterprise pursuits with no sales engineers, legal, or executive sponsors.
The user prefers long narrative essays about industry history in sales proposals with no pricing tables, scope, or implementation timeline.
The user always chooses the cheapest fast-food options for client entertainment and avoids venues appropriate to deal size.
The user prefers extremely blunt one-line demand cold outreach emails with no personalization, value proposition, or polite opening.
The user always keeps pipeline deals in a single generic stage with no forecast categories, close dates, or activity logging.
The user writes CRM opportunity notes as single-word bullet labels with no context on buyer pain, stakeholders, or next actions.
The user always leads negotiations with the lowest possible discount and ignores value-based pricing, packaging, or multi-year terms.
The user prefers passive indirect phrasing in post-demo follow-up emails with no clear next step, meeting request, or deadline.
The user always skips discovery calls for new opportunities and jumps straight to contract send.
